title: A new convert is clean, but not all, and must keep repenting
setting: William E. McLellin, a recent convert from Paris, Illinois, met Joseph Smith at a conference in Orange, Ohio, on 25–26 October 1831. He then traveled with Joseph to Hiram, arriving on 29 October. McLellin had privately asked the Lord five questions, which he never recorded. At his request, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation that day, probably in the John Johnson home. McLellin wrote it down and said it answered his questions fully.
summary: The voice in verse 1 speaks as the Redeemer to William McLellin and blesses him for turning from his sins and receiving the everlasting covenant. It says he is clean, “but not all,” and must repent of what the Lord will show him. He is to preach from land to land where the gospel has not been heard. He is not to go to Zion yet, but to the eastern lands with Samuel Smith. He is to lay hands on the sick, be patient in affliction, and not be cumbered. It warns him against adultery, a temptation that has troubled him. If he continues to the end, he will receive a crown of eternal life.

contextNote.title: Clean, but not all
contextNote.text: McLellin had silently asked questions he never wrote down. JSP editors think one concern was his standing before God. Verse 1 blesses him for turning away from his sins. Verse 3 then limits the blessing: he is clean, “but not all.” The same verse promises the Lord will show him what still needs repenting. Verse 10 names one such matter, a temptation to adultery. In this passage, being clean is real but partial, and the remedy is ongoing repentance.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 64–66 sees in this revelation the Lord’s personal care for one man. Verse 3 calls McLellin “clean, but not all”; which instructions in verses 9–12 would help him finish that work?
reviewNote: Read all 13 verses. Official heading gives Hiram, 29 October 1831, and McLellin’s five secret questions. JSP historical introduction gave the Orange conference, travel to Hiram, the probable room in the Johnson home, and McLellin’s satisfaction. Orange, Ohio, and Paris, Illinois, are setting details only and were not added as places. independence stands for “the land of Zion” in v. 6. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary changed 'heal the sick' to 'lay hands on the sick' to match verse 9.
